adapters.label: Apple Notes
adapters.accepts: Apple Notes — recognised, but Notes has no export file to give us.
adapters.block: Apple Notes has no export format at all: there is no 'download your notes' file, and the notes themselves live in an Apple-internal database that is not readable outside the app. Two routes work. In the Notes app, select a note and use File → Export as PDF, which gives one PDF per note that this server reads as a document. Or run a local tool such as Exporter or apple-notes-exporter, which walks the app and writes one Markdown file per note into a folder — drop that folder here and every note becomes a row with its title and its text.

adapters.label: Calendar (.ics)
adapters.accepts: An .ics calendar file — from Google Takeout, Apple Calendar or Outlook.

adapters.label: Confluence space export (HTML)
adapters.accepts: The Confluence-space-export-….html.zip from a space's HTML export.

adapters.label: Folder of documents
adapters.accepts: Any folder or .zip of documents — .txt, .md, .pdf, .docx, .html, .rtf, .csv.

adapters.label: Mail message files (.eml)
adapters.accepts: A single .eml message, or a folder or .zip full of them.

adapters.label: Evernote export (.enex)
adapters.accepts: An .enex file — Evernote's 'Export notes' output, one file per notebook.

adapters.label: Facebook data export (JSON)
adapters.accepts: The JSON .zip from Facebook's 'Download your information'.

adapters.label: Gmail / mail archive (.mbox)
adapters.accepts: A .mbox file — from Google Takeout, Thunderbird, Apple Mail or Fastmail.

adapters.label: Google Takeout
adapters.accepts: The .zip or .tgz Google emails you after a Takeout — Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Chat and YouTube history in one drop.

adapters.label: iMessage (chat.db)
adapters.accepts: iMessage history — recognised, but it has to be exported off the Mac first.
adapters.block: iMessage keeps its history in a SQLite database called chat.db inside the Mac's protected Library folder, which macOS does not let an app or a server read — not even with your password — and which is not a file Apple lets you hand over directly. The route is to get the conversations out of the Messages app yourself: open a conversation, select the messages and use File → Print → Save as PDF, or use a local exporter such as iMazing or imessage-exporter to write the chat to a .txt or .html file. Drop that file here and the conversation reads like any other chat export.

adapters.label: Instagram data export (JSON)
adapters.accepts: The JSON .zip from Instagram's 'Download your information'.

adapters.label: Kindle highlights (My Clippings.txt)
adapters.accepts: The 'My Clippings.txt' file from your Kindle's documents folder.

adapters.label: LinkedIn data export
adapters.accepts: The .zip LinkedIn emails you after 'Get a copy of your data'.

adapters.label: Medium / Substack export
adapters.accepts: The .zip from Medium's 'Download your information' or Substack's export.

adapters.label: Notion workspace export
adapters.accepts: The Export-….zip Notion emails you after 'Export all workspace content'.

adapters.label: Outlook message files (.msg)
adapters.accepts: Outlook .msg files — recognised, but they need converting first.
adapters.block: An Outlook .msg file is not text: it is a Microsoft compound OLE2 storage document, the same container format as an old .doc, with the headers, body and attachments stored as separate binary streams inside it. Reading it needs a converter rather than a parser. In Outlook, select the messages and use File → Open & Export → Import/Export → 'Export to a file' to write a .pst, or drag the messages out as .eml; a .pst can then be turned into an mbox with readpst (libpff), and this server reads both mbox and .eml today.

adapters.label: Outlook mailbox (.pst / .ost)
adapters.accepts: Outlook .pst or .ost mailboxes — recognised, but they need converting first.
adapters.block: A .pst or .ost file is a whole Outlook mailbox packed into one Microsoft compound storage file, with the folder tree, every message and every attachment held as binary records inside it — there is no text to read without unpacking it first. Two routes work today. In Outlook, use File → Open & Export → Import/Export → 'Export to a file' to write a .pst, then convert it with readpst (the libpff tools) which turns each folder into an mbox file. Or, if the mailbox is still live, ask Google Takeout or your mail provider for an mbox directly. This server reads the converted mbox today, and an .ost must be converted the same way because Outlook will not open one from another machine.

adapters.label: Readwise highlights (CSV)
adapters.accepts: The CSV from Readwise's Export page — every highlight and note you kept.

adapters.label: Reddit data request
adapters.accepts: The .zip Reddit emails you after a data request — your posts and comments.

adapters.label: Slack workspace export
adapters.accepts: The .zip Slack emails you after a workspace export.

adapters.label: Microsoft Teams / Purview eDiscovery export
adapters.accepts: A Purview eDiscovery export of Teams messages — it needs converting first.
adapters.block: A Microsoft Teams export does not contain Teams messages as text. Purview eDiscovery packages the conversations as Outlook .pst mailboxes beside a manifest file (Manifest.xml or results.csv) that lists what is in them, so reading it is the same problem as reading a .pst. Convert the .pst files with readpst (the libpff tools), which writes one mbox per folder, and drop those here — this server reads mbox today and each Teams conversation arrives as its own thread.

adapters.label: Telegram chat export (JSON)
adapters.accepts: The result.json (or its folder/zip) from Telegram Desktop's chat export.

adapters.label: TikTok data export (JSON)
adapters.accepts: The JSON .zip from TikTok's 'Download your data'.

adapters.label: Meeting transcript (vtt / srt / txt)
adapters.accepts: A .vtt, .srt or Otter/Fireflies .txt transcript — one file or a folder of them.

adapters.label: WhatsApp chat export
adapters.accepts: The .txt (or the .zip with media) that WhatsApp's 'Export chat' sends you.

adapters.label: X / Twitter archive
adapters.accepts: The .zip X sends you from Settings → 'Download an archive of your data'.

adapters.label: Zoom local recordings folder
adapters.accepts: A Zoom recordings folder — the audio needs transcribing, not parsing.
adapters.block: A Zoom local recordings folder holds the meeting itself — an .mp4 video and an .m4a audio file — plus the in-meeting chat as a .txt. The video and audio are not text and no parser can read words out of them; they have to be transcribed, which is a different job from reading an export and runs on the transcription lane rather than here. Two routes: turn on 'Audio transcript' in Zoom's cloud-recording settings and re-download the meeting, which gives you a .vtt this server reads as a transcript, or send the .m4a through transcription first. The chat .txt in the folder can be dropped here today.
